subject.title: Telegram: per-chat lane serialization (isolated ingress) starves messages.queue.collect — same-chat bursts never coalesce

question: Should busy same-lane Telegram spooled updates be admitted into the active reply operation's collect/follow-up queue, or should Telegram keep strict per-chat serialization even though same-chat `collect` then cannot coalesce bursts?
rationale: The source issue is clear, but the fix crosses the Telegram durable spool/drain boundary and the core reply queue contract, where ordering, replay, retry, and control-lane behavior are product and reliability choices.

options.title: Bridge Busy Lanes Into Collect
options.body: Add a Telegram-aware admission path that lets compatible same-lane spooled updates join the active follow-up queue while preserving spool durability and lane/control invariants.

options.title: Document Telegram Limitation
options.body: Keep strict same-lane serialization and explicitly document that same-chat Telegram bursts do not use `collect` under isolated ingress.

options.title: Defer To Shared Ingress Design
options.body: Leave this as the canonical design item until maintainers define a shared ingress-to-dispatch contract instead of a Telegram-only bridge.

recommendation.title: Bridge Busy Lanes Into Collect
recommendation.body: Add a Telegram-aware admission path that lets compatible same-lane spooled updates join the active follow-up queue while preserving spool durability and lane/control invariants.
